Document.project_name: Restoration of Canning Field Road
location: Kejimkujik National Park and  National Historic Site
Document.description:
A 2km gravel road with ingrown needs to be restored to a safe, serviceable condition. The parks Canada assets team will clear the adjacent road vegetation in the fall of 2026. The grading and roadbed restoration work will be contracted out and it will consist of the following: 
1. Road Grading
• Grade the full length (approximately 2 km) of the gravel road.
• Restore the road profile to promote positive surface drainage by establishing an appropriate crown and eliminating low spots, potholes, wash boarding, and other surface irregularities.
• Shape the road to ensure water is directed away from the travelled surface and does not pond on the roadway.
2. Roadbed Restoration
• Re-establish the existing roadbed by reclaiming and reshaping suitable existing road materials.
• Any organic material encountered during grading, including sod, vegetation, roots, topsoil, or other unsuitable materials brought to the surface, shall be removed from the roadway and properly disposed of off the travelled surface.
• Organic materials shall not be buried within the reconstructed roadbed.
3. Supply and Placement of Aggregate
• Supply and deliver approximately 150 cubic yards of Class A aggregate.
• Spread and uniformly distribute the aggregate over the road in locations necessary to restore the driving surface and maintain the required road profile.
• Blend the new aggregate with the existing road material as required to achieve a consistent surface.
4. Compaction
• Following grading and placement of the new aggregate, compact the entire treated roadway using suitable compaction equipment.
• Compaction shall produce a firm, stable, and uniform driving surface free of rutting, loose material, or displacement.

Document.project_name: Hydro One Orléans Area Reinforcement
location: Between Hydro One's Hawthorne Transformer Station (TS) and Orléans TS in Ottawa

Document.project_name: Construction and expansion of buildings in Houston, Texas, USA
Document.description:
Compass Energy Systems Inc. is requesting financing from BDC for the construction of a new building and the expansion of an existing building on its property located at 4444 Brittmoore Road, Houston, Texas, USA. The site is approximately 117,359 m² in size and is currently occupied by eight buildings totalling 24,332 m². No trees or vegetation will need to be removed. Concrete foundations will need to be added.

The total footprint of the new building and expansion will be approximately 1,672 m². Compass Energy Systems Inc. manufactures and assembles high-performance compression, process and power system packages. The new building and expansion will be used to increase its current capacity.

The new building will be used for the assembly of components for the power and natural gas compression industry. The majority of the operations will be the assembly of equipment from external manufacturers or internally completed pipe and vessels. Some on skid welding will be done but minimal, pipe fitting, electrical and instrumentation installation as well for the control systems.

The expansion will be an additional large paint booth to the existing facility, but with a free standing chimney. Required permits are under review.

Document.project_name: Antenna Structure Foundation Replacement – NRS Aldergrove
Document.description: The Department of National Defence (DND) is proposing a project. Primary work will focus on foundation replacement for existing structures due to water degradation of structural guy foundations and replacement of temporary anchorage put in place in 2023. The anchor point replacement will begin with the antenna curtains being lowered to the ground; then work will proceed with the dismantling of one tower at a time and the release of each of the three anchor points associated with that particular tower, the first frame of the tower will remain in place. The existing anchor points will be excavated, old concrete removed and new concrete foundations formed and poured. The blocks for the temporary anchor points will be disassembled and stored on site.

Document.project_name: Sikh-E-Dakh (Glen Vowell Band) - Sik-E-Dakh Wastewater System
location: Sikh-E-Dakh (Glen Vowell Band) - Sik-E-Dakh Wastewater System
Document.description: The project includes a community sanitary sewer collection system, a lift station, a lagoon based wastewater treatment system and an outfall to the Skeena River. The project is designed for a maximum discharge to the Skeena River of 1359 m3/day. The expected lifespan of the facility is 50 years. The project construction footprint is 115,696m2. The Sikh-E-Dakh (Glen Vowell Band) has applied to Fisheries and Oceans Canada (DFO) for a Fisheries Act Authorization and for funding from Indigenous Services Canada's Community Infrastructure program for the construction of the proposed project. The proposed site for the project is on the Skeena River on Sikh-E-Dakh reserve land.

Document.project_name: Lytton First Nation - Stein Water System Intake Improvements Project
location: Lytton First Nation - Stein Water System Intake Improvements Project
Document.description:
The Lytton Creek wildfire in June of 2021 resulted in the destruction of residences in the Lytton First Nation (LFN) community, impacting LFN community members. Subsequent reconstruction and subdivision to accommodate the destroyed homes has resulted in planning for additional development within the community. Although there is an existing water intake on Stein River that currently feeds the Water Treatment Plant, it is nearing the end of its service life and design capacity and requires replacement to meet the growing needs of the community as it rebuilds.
	The existing raw water intake and Booster Station 1 do not provide adequate capacity for the growing and migrating population.
	The installation of a new intake from the Stein River, as well as a small booster station and alignment of the watermain to connect the new intake to the existing system is being proposed.

Document.project_name: Annapolis Royal Living Shoreline
location: Fort Anne National Historic Site of Canada
Document.description: The Annapolis Royal Living Shoreline Project is a coastal restoration initiative that will restore a salt marsh degraded by long-term development along the Annapolis Royal waterfront, using a living shoreline approach to strengthen shoreline resilience and intertidal ecosystems. The restored salt marsh will reduce erosion and wave energy, helping stabilize the shoreline and support future climate adaptation. It will also enhance habitat for invertebrates, fish, and birds. The existing marsh will remain intact, with the marsh footprint extended seaward. Project works include rearranging existing armour stone, supplemented with imported stone as required, to create a series of inner and outer protective rock sills along the waterfront spanning from approximately 83 meters south of Annapolis Royal Wharf to Queen's Wharf, without impacting the wharf itself. Although the broader project occurs along municipal waterfront lands, this basic impact assessment considers the works proposed on Parks Canada land. These works are limited to the placement of one inner and one outer rock sill, along with a small overlapping section of a third and fourth sill, as well as associated marsh substrate between the inner sill and existing marsh. No construction access through Parks Canada upland property is proposed. Construction is planned for fall 2026, with planting and post-construction monitoring continuing into 2027.

Document.project_name: Crawford Nickel Project
Document.description: Canada Nickel Company is proposing the construction, operation, decommissioning and abandonment of an open-pit nickel-cobalt mine and on-site metal mill, located 42 kilometres north of Timmins, Ontario. As proposed, the Crawford Nickel Project would have a mine ore production capacity of 240,000 tonnes per day and a mill ore input capacity of 120,000 tonnes per day. The project would operate for about 41 years.

Document.project_name: Shoal Lake 40 First Nation Wastewater Treatment System
Document.description:
The project will involve the construction of a wastewater treatment system which will utilize Submerged Attached Growth Reactor (SAGR) treatment cells, with a grinder, microscreen, clarification, and UV disinfection located inside a proposed 380 square meter building. The treatment system will accept both hauled sewage from the existing septic tanks in the community and collected wastewater from piped services for future housing developments, designed for 20 years. A generator will be installed on the premises in case of power outages. The total footprint for development is approximately 10,000 square meters including the proposed buildling, SAGR cells, driveway, upgrades to the access road, waterwaste piping and borrow area.

The discharge of the system will be an above-ground outfall located adjacent to a wetland which connects to Snowshoe Bay in Shoal Lake. Shoal Lake is used as a drinking water source for the community and Winnipeg. The intakes for both these systems are in Indian Bay, on the opposite side of the Shoal Lake 40 peninsula. The treated effluent is expected to meet all effluent guidelines and not impact the water quality of Shoal Lake.

This project is in association with support from Infrastructure Canada's posting #89407.

Document.project_name: Frog Lake Cree Nation New Water Service Line
Document.description:
Frog Lake Cree Nation intends to construct a new water service line. The water line will run from the existing Frog Lake Cree Nation water treatment plant, then follows Highway 897 to tie into the proposed wrap around services building. The HDPE pipeline will be approximately 3.5 km in length and will be installed via open cut or directional drilling methods where appropriate.

The Project will require vegetation removal and grubbing. The clearing area is approximately 17 500 square metres and post construction vegetation will be seeded to restore the project footprint to stabilized conditions. Vegetation clearing will be strictly limited to the proposed project area and a wildlife / nesting sweep of this area will be completed prior to the onset of clearing activities will be completed in accordance with indigenous and federal standards and regulations. Appropriate buffers setback distances will be established should any active nests be found during the sweep by a qualified wildlife specialist. The Project is not located within any sensitive wildlife zones or critical habitat.

Indigenous Services Canada is providing funding in support of the Project.

Document.project_name: Stage 1 - Harvey Jimmy Compound Project (HJCP) – CFB Kingston
Document.description: The Department of National Defence (DND) is proposing a project. The Harvey Jimmy Compound Project modernizes a section of the Harvey Training Area at Canadian Forces Base (CFB) Kingston to address critical infrastructure gaps limiting Signals and Technician training at Canadian Forces School of Communications and Electronics (CFSCE). Current deficiencies in power, communications, hardstand, and network integration restrict training realism, throughput, and compliance across the school. The project will deliver permanent power, expanded hardstand, communications towers, and fibre connectivity to enable concurrent, high-fidelity field training. The area will have generators and Special Equipment Vehicle/Special Equipment Systems (SEV/SES) containers to enable austere simulation. Phase 1 of the project will include the construction of an approximately 3700 m2 gravel pad to incorporate and support training infrastructure and equipment.

Document.project_name: Town of Banff 26DP48 408 Marten Street Development
Document.description: The proponent proposes to construct a four-storey residential building containing 23 dwelling units at 408 Marten Street. The development will include:, building construction, installation of utilities, site landscaping, creation of 3 parking stalls and bike storage. Demolition is not included in this scope, as it was already completed under a separate impact assessment.

Document.project_name: Northgate-Riding Mountain National Park Trail Expansion
location: Riding Mountain National Park of Canada
Document.description: Riding Mountain National Park is considering a proposal from an external client, The Northgate Trails Inc., who are proposing a new, multi-use stacked trail system that will establish a formal connection with the existing Northgate Trail Network (26 km) located adjacent to the park. Construction will include 25 km of new trail built using sustainable trail construction best practices. A combination of raised-tread and bench-cut trail construction methods will be used to suit site-specific terrain and environmental conditions. In addition, the existing 5 km Crawford Creek Trail will be upgraded primarily to raised-tread construction to enhance trail sustainability, durability, and overall user experience. The upgraded Crawford Creek Trail will serve as the primary climbing route, with new sustainable trail loops providing multiple descent options back to the trailhead. Green trails will peel off sooner with less climbing and gentler grades. Several blue trails will peel off at higher elevations. The steepest climbing is encountered along the last kilometer of the climb trail and will provide experienced trail users with a longer wilderness experience with a very remote feeling. The stacked-loop trail system is designed to support user progression, accommodate a broader range of skill levels, and appeal to multiple user groups. The west side of the network will be designed as a multi-use trail system optimized for mountain biking, while the east side will support cross-country skiing.

Document.project_name: Town of Banff 26DP49 410 Banff Avenue Housing Development
Document.description: The project proposed is for the demolition of an existing single detached home at 410 Banff Avenue, and the construction of a 5-unit multiplex with 5-bedrooms per unit. All structures and vegetation currently on the property (home, shed, trees) will be removed. The new building will be 4 storeys and will include a basement unit, but no underground parking garage. The timeline is unknown.

Document.project_name: Joyce Lake Direct Shipping Iron Ore Project
location: Labrador (approximately 20 km northeast of Schefferville, QC)
Document.description:
Joyce Direct Iron Inc. is proposing the construction, operation and decommissioning of an open-pit iron ore mine located in Newfoundland and Labrador, approximately 20 kilometres northeast of Schefferville, Quebec. As proposed, the mine would produce up to an estimated 2.5 million tons of ore per year over a life span of seven years. The project would consist of an open pit mine, dewatering of Joyce Lake, crushing and screening of ore (dry processing), waste rock disposal, support infrastructure, access and haulage roads, a causeway, and a rail loop to connect with an existing railway.

Please note that the proponent for this project was formerly Labec Century Iron Ore Inc.

Document.project_name: Building Adaptation Project – Rideau Hall, Ottawa, ON
Brandon Dispatchable Capacity Project
location: East Brandon Industrial Area within the City of Brandon
Document.description: Manitoba Hydro is proposing the expansion of an existing natural gas-fueled electricity generating facility, located in Brandon, Manitoba. As proposed, the Brandon Dispatchable Capacity Project would include the development of three new simple-cycle combustion turbines, with an anticipated increase in production capacity of approximately 750 megawatts. Project components would also include a 32-kilometre natural gas pipeline, two electrical transmission lines totalling 3.5 kilometres, and upgrades to the existing electrical transmission station. The project is expected to operate for about 30 years.

Document.project_name: Installation of a new dock at the Saint-Anne-de-Bellevue Canal
location: Sainte-Anne-de-Bellevue Canal National Historic Site of Canada
Document.description: The project consists of installing a new floating dock upstream from the Canal-de-Sainte-Anne-de-Bellevue lock. The dock consists of six sections, each measuring 40 feet by 8 feet, for a total length of 240 feet. It will be positioned along the pier wall and parallel to the navigation channel. The installation will be carried out using two anchoring systems. The first sections will be attached to the concrete wall of the pier, while the sections extending beyond the end of the pier will be held in place by a deadweight and chain anchoring system.

Document.project_name: Town of Banff Trail Lighting: Rec Grounds & Glen to Spray Ave.
Document.description: The Town of Banff is proposing to install bollard trail lighting: along Glen Avenue to Spray Avenue to complete the nighttime route connection between the Muskrat St pedestrian bridge and Spray Ave. from the Nancy Pauw pedestrian bridge along the paved central pathway in the Recreation Grounds to the pavilion. Construction will consist mainly of shallow trenching for electrical conduit installation, local excavations for the concrete bases for each bollard, backfilling, and electrical work.

Document.project_name: Replacement of the St. Jean Garrison gas station
Document.description: The Department of National Defence (DND) is proposing a project. The project consists of removing seven underground storage tanks that have reached the end of their service life and replacing the old service station at the Saint-Jean-sur-Richelieu Garrison with a new facility featuring two aboveground storage tanks, each with a capacity of 25,000 L.

Document.project_name: Emerald Lake Road Rock Scaling
Document.description: The project involves direct and indirect slope stabilization works, including scaling, removal of scaled material from ditches, and tree debris removal along the upper slopes of Emerald Lake Road. This project is required to address engineer identified areas along the Category 4 road between the Trans Canada Highway and Emerald Lake. Emerald Lake is popular for visitors, with overnight and day users frequently driving the road and stopping. Slope stabilization is required as routine maintenance to this corridor to provide increased road safety to staff and visitors using these areas.

Document.project_name: Integrated Climate Adaptation Solutions for the Hindu Kush Himalaya (HI-CAS) -Bhutan
Document.proponent: International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD)
Document.description: The Integrated Climate Adaptation Solutions for the Hindu Kush Himalaya Region (HI-CAS) is a regional project implemented in Bangladesh, Bhutan, and Nepal funded by Global Affairs Canada (GAC) and implemented by the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD) in partnership with the Tarayana Foundation in Bhutan. The project aims to improve climate-resilient, nature-positive livelihoods while strengthening the leadership and agency of rural women and Indigenous Peoples and Local Communities (IPLCs). The project will deliver locally tailored climate adaptation solutions that are grounded in feminist and human rights-based methodologies thus ensuring an inclusive approach that place the rights, agency, and leadership of IPLCs at the centre. These evidence-informed Integrated Adaptation Solution Packages (IASPs) will combine springshed management, renewable energy technologies for power irrigation systems, and agrobiodiversity practices. They will be complemented by capacity building and knowledge sharing to drive institutional policy and action and to attract sustainable investments in climate action and development, particularly in the water, energy, and agrobiodiversity sectors, with a strong focus on the leadership of women and IPLCs.

Document.project_name: Wharf 401 Reconstruction - Millerand Harbour - Magdalen Islands
Document.proponent: Small Craft Harbours  - Fisheries and Oceans Canada
Document.description:
A recent underwater inspection revealed extensive deterioration of exposed wooden com-ponents and bolted assemblies. New cladding or ladders can no longer be safely installed due to the advanced degradation of the existing wood.

Built in 1974, the structure has exceeded its intended lifespan, and partial repairs are no longer viable. A full reconstruction of Wharf 401 is required to ensure the safety of vessels and fishermans.

 
The project includes the following activities:

•    Supply of treated timber, plastic cladding, galvanized hardware, concrete slabs, and ballast stone
•    Partial demolition of the existing creosote treated timber cribwork
•    Proper disposal of demolition materials, including treated and creo-sote contaminated wood
•    Excavation of the seabed to prepare a granular foundation for new cribwork
•    Assembly, launching, placement, and completion of timber cribwork structures
•    Installation of precast concrete slabs, ladders, and fenders
•    Electrical and mechanical upgrades to modernize wharf services

Document.project_name: Wharf 403 Reconstruction - Newport Harbour - Gaspésie
Document.proponent: Small Craft Harbours  - Fisheries and Oceans Canada
Document.description:
Wharf 403, constructed in the late 1980s has reached the end of its service life and now exhibits significant structural deterioration. Steel fasteners are heavily corroded and the timber components have degraded, leading to the closure of the wharf to vehicular traffic for several years.


Similarly, the timber crib section of Wharf 401, which dates back to the 1960s, has exceeded its useful lifespan. Reconstructing these structures is essential to maintaining operational capacity within the harbour.


The project will ensure continued support for the snow crab fishery, provide berthing capacity for vessels from the FMP Shipyard, and maintain the harbour's ability to accommodate a potential future Canadian Coast Guard base. Restoring these wharves will return full functionality to this strategic area of the harbour.

This project includes the following activities:


•Demolition of deteriorated treated-timber and concrete structures, with proper disposal of materials.
•Removal of the existing breakwater and recovery of reusable stone.
•Supply and installation of treated timber, plastic siding, galvanized hardware, and concrete slabs for new timber cribs.
•Supply of crushed stone for crib foundations.
•Installation of armour stone and filter stone for riprap protection along the new wharves.

Document.project_name: False Creek Small Craft Harbour Limited Sediment Remediation and Tidal Boat Grid Removal
location: False Creek Harbour, Vancouver, 1505 West 1st Avenue, Vancouver, V6J 1E8
Document.description:
The Project is located in False Creek Inlet in Vancouver, British Columbia. Work to decommission the southern active boat grid and remediate the sediment in the northern grid of the False Creek Small Craft Harbour falls within the mandate of the Federal Contaminated Sites Action Plan to reduce environmental and human health risks from known federal contaminated sites.

Tidal grids were typically used for vessel maintenance during low tide periods and these maintenance activities have the potential to introduce contamination into the surrounding sediments. Previous Environmental Site Assessments found Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons, Tributyltin, and metals exceedances of applicable environmental criteria within the area of the boat grid.

The boat grids are occasionally used by harbour users. The southern grid will continue to be available for use after the sediment surrounding the grid is removed and disposed of in a provincially licensed receiving facility. The northern grid will be decommissioned and the surrounding sediment will also be disposed of in a provincially licensed receiving facility. Work will be completed using a long-reach excavator from shore.

Remediation will address contamination in the sediments within the area of the existing boat grid.  The excavation footprint is anticipated to be 15-30 cubic meters per grid. Work will be completed following Fisheries and Oceans Canada's best standards of practise to minimize adverse effects to fish and fish habitat.

Work is expected to start in mid July to align with day time seasonal low-tide windows and take 1 week.

Document.project_name: Replacement of Employee Residences at Chief Mountain Port of Entry
Document.description: The Canada Border Services Agency is proposing to replace the existing employee residences at the Chief Mountain Port of Entry, located within Waterton Lakes National Park. The project will involve the demolition and removal of five aging housing units that have reached the end of their service life. The replacement staff residences will be constructed using modular components fabricated off-site and transported to the location for installation. Existing utilities, water supply, and the septic system will be reused where feasible or replaced as needed to support the new infrastructure.

Document.project_name: Boundary Fence Upgrades - Kesler Lake and Highway 6 to the Waterton River
location: Waterton Lakes National Park of Canada
Document.description: Parks Canada proposes two boundary fence improvement components in Waterton Lakes National Park: approximately 1.2 km of new fencing around Kesler Lake and approximately 1.3 km of drill stem fencing from Highway 6 to the Waterton River that will replace the existing cattle exclusion fence. The Kesler Lake component follows a new alignment and will require localized vegetation clearing, though use of existing open areas along the alignment will be prioritized. The drill stem component follows the existing boundary fence alignment and disturbance footprint, and no vegetation clearing is anticipated. This section serves as a pilot installation to evaluate the durability of drill stem as a fence material on the existing boundary fence alignment and its potential effects on wildlife movement. Both fence designs will be bison-resistant yet permeable to other wildlife.

Document.project_name: LaPointe Pier Repairs - GCT Vanterm
Document.description:
Legacy Environmental on behalf of Global Container Terminals Inc. proposes to conduct maintenance and structural rehabilitation of the LaPointe Pier located at GCT Vanterm in Burrard Inlet, Vancouver. The works are required to address localized failure and ongoing corrosion of sheet piles along the pier, including approximately 40 metres of collapsed sheet piles that have reduced berth depth and compromised structural integrity. The objective is to restore berth functionality, maintain safe operations, and stabilize existing infrastructure without expanding the footprint of the pier.

Proposed in-water works include removal of collapsed sheet piles from the seabed, installation of approximately 75 square metres of gabion baskets along the western pier face, and placement of approximately 490 square metres of riprap at the northeast corner of the structure. Additional activities may include re-securing existing sheet piles with anchor rods and steel strapping, installation of corrosion protection anodes, and underwater welding and drilling associated with these repairs.

Construction will be undertaken using divers working from the pier and/or a barge-mounted crane, with supporting equipment such as hydraulic tools, welding equipment, and material placement from barge or land-based staging. Works will proceed in phases including demolition/removal, inspection, installation of stabilization measures, and armouring. In-water works are anticipated to occur over approximately 10 weeks.

Document.project_name: Rehabilitation of Wharves 78 and 79, Davie Shipyard
Gatineau River Shoreline Pathway Modification
Installation of Automated Gates in Gatineau Park
Rehabilitation of the Touraine wastewater pumping station
Document.description:
The project consists of the complete rehabilitation of the Touraine wastewater pumping station. The Touraine pumping station is located within the territory of the City of Gatineau, in the Outaouais administrative region (Quebec).

The work at the Touraine wastewater pumping station is necessary to ensure its long-term proper functioning. The City must improve how it measures the water entering the station to comply with the standards of the Ministry of Environment, Fight Against Climate Change, Wildlife and Parks (MELCCFP) regarding overflows. This will allow measuring the amount of water that overflows (by comparing the water entering with that which is pumped). To obtain a reliable measurement, water must flow regularly before reaching the measuring device (the Parshall flume). To achieve this, the inlet pipe must be rebuilt over a distance of approximately 9 meters. The City of Gatineau will also take advantage of this work to install a bypass pipe to facilitate maintenance work (cleaning, repairs, and others) of the sanitary well. The new bypass pipe would help prevent overflows into the river during these maintenance works.

The chosen solution is to build the bypass chamber and the channel in the current location of the sanitary pipe to minimize the ground space used. The generator will be installed on land that has already been developed. A gravel access road will be constructed to the north to access the pumping station on land owned by Hydro-Québec. The City has obtained Hydro-Québec's authorization for this road.

Federal approval for land use from the NCC (National Capital Commission) is required as part of the project affects its lands. Coordination with the Canadian Wildlife Service (CWS) of Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) is necessary because the CWS must issue a permit under the Species at Risk Act for work planned in the essential habitat of the Western Chorus Frog. For this project to proceed, ECCC must make a decision under the Impact Assessment Act. This department is a signatory authority along with the NCC.

The sequence of activities for the Touraine pumping station project is as follows:

1.         A temporary pumping pipe will be installed on the surface, between the Touraine pumping station and the existing inspection chamber of the sanitary pipe serving the Touraine areanear Leamy Creek. It will divert wastewater from the inlet channel directly to the station's effluent to be sent to the Gatineau wastewater treatment plant. It will operate until the end of the pumping station rehabilitation work or as needed and will be dismantled afterward.

2.         The contractor will excavate to install infrastructure related to the treatment plant, including the bypass chamber and the generator. The soil will be restored with the existing material and clean fill. Grass will also be seeded (hydraulic seeding type 1 (H1)) and shrubs planted (at least three native species).

3.         To reduce erosion of the Leamy Creek banks, a culvert will be installed along the northsouth axis of the planned road to the Touraine pumping station, and an existing culvert will be extended along the east-west axis. It is also planned to install two retention berms during the work to manage sediment transport to the watercourse.

Project activities will take place over a period of 10 weeks, divided into 3 phases between early August 2025 and late November 2027.

Document.project_name: Redevelopment of a portion of the Luskville Falls trail in Gatineau Park
On-Farm Composting System, Pilot Project
Document.description: This pilot project proposes the establishment of an on farm composting system to help address orchard waste management challenges. Project will reduce landfill hauling requirements, and improve sustainability and nutrient cycling on-farm. Project will involve the installation of approximately 200 meters of electric fence and gate, as well as approximately 200 meters of underground pipeline to distribute water to the area from an existing source.

Document.project_name: Beardy's & Okemasis Cree Nation Landfill Access Road Repairs
location: BEARDY'S AND OKEMASIS INDIAN RESERVE NO. 96 & 97
Document.description:
The proposed project involves the upgrade of three access roads leading to the Beardy's & Okemasis Cree Nation landfill in Saskatchewan. The road improvements are required to support the safe and efficient transport of materials during the planned decommissioning of the landfill. Construction will consist of upgrades to existing roadway infrastructure, including road surfacing and ditching upgrades to approximately 1.6 km of existing road 604, 1.6 km of existing landfill access road 611, and 300 m of existing landfill road 835.

Construction activities will be carried out in two phases. Road surface upgrades are scheduled for completion by September 1, 2026. Ditch construction and associated works will occur between September 2 and October 31, 2026, to avoid impacts during the bird nesting season of the region, which concludes on September 1.

All anticipated waste generated during construction activities will be responsibly managed and disposed of to a designated landfill facility. in addition, procedures will be implemented throughout construction to prevent potential contamination from petroleum products used for on-site equipment.

Document.project_name: Fort Frontenac Shore Wall Repair – Kingston
Document.description: The Department of National Defence (DND) is proposing a project. The proposed undertaking involves the rehabilitation of an existing concrete seawall at Fort Frontenac in Kingston, Ontario. The project will include the installation of a rock berm along the base of the wall to provide structural reinforcement, the localized removal and replacement of a deteriorated section of the wall, and the filling of voids of the existing structure with grout or concrete. Construction activities will involve in-water work, which will be isolated using turbidity curtains, and all concrete works will be appropriately contained to prevent environmental contamination. Once construction is complete, the seawall will return to passive operation, functioning as a stable shoreline structure that requires no active maintenance or mechanical operation. Site restoration will involve backfilling with clear stone, as well as the stabilization of disturbed areas to restore the shoreline to its pre-construction condition. The entire project is expected to be completed by the end of 2026, with no long-term adverse environmental effects anticipated.

Document.project_name: Modification of Underground Marine Pipelines at Section 70 of the Port of Montreal, Borough of Mercier-Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, Montreal, Quebec
Solid-waste Infrastructure Expansion - Tataskweyak Cree Nation
Document.description:
Tataskweyak Cree Nation in northern Manitoba is proposing to expand the community landfill. This expansion is a critical infrastructure project, as the existing landfill has reached capacity and can no longer adequately serve the community's needs.

The Project will require vegetation clearing and excavation next to the existing landfill. The Project will take place on reserve land (Split Lake No.171) which is home to Tataskweyak Cree Nation. The Project has requirements under section 82 of the Impact Assessment Act (IAA).

Document.project_name: Valley Fiber Limited Radiocommunication Tower on Fairford First Nation Reserve No. 50
Document.description: Valley Fiber Limited is proposing a new 59 metre radiocommunication tower located on the Fairford First Nation Reserve No. 50. The tower will be built to improve network access of high-speed internet to the community's businesses and members. It will include guy-wire anchors and two sets of four-sector antennas. In the future, the tower may have other antennas and other radiocommunication equipment added or replaced.

Document.project_name: Linden Terrace Storm Sewer Upgrades, Ottawa
Residential and Institutional Development, South Amishk Sector - Pekuakamiulnuatsh Takuhikan
Bischof Islands Float Camp Rehabilitation
location: Gwaii Haanas National Park Reserve and Haida Heritage Site of Canada
Document.description: Parks Canada is proposing repair work at the Bischoff Islands float camp, which serves as a central logistical hub for operations throughout Gwaii Haanas. The float camp consists of two housing floats and two support floats and has been in service at its current location since 2015. No new structures will be added, and there will be no increase in footprint below the high-water mark. The project will include repairs to the flotation, moorage, float connections, walkways, and interior and exterior structures to improve safety and extend service life. Work will involve removing marine growth from the underside of existing foam flotation and installing a protective barrier beneath the floats; replacing existing moorage components, anchors, float-to-float connections, and bull rails; replacing interior drywall with a marine-suitable alternative; installing two incinerator toilets and associated plumbing upgrades; reconstructing walkways; and adding flotation to level the existing floats. Work occurring in water will undergo Fisheries and Oceans Canada review to ensure appropriate mitigation measures for the marine environment.

Document.project_name: Sage Meadow Development Phase 1A Infrastructure Works
Mooring pile installations - Seaspan's Vancouver Shipyards
location: Mooring pile installations - Seaspan's Vancouver Shipyards
Document.description:
As part of Canada's National Shipbuilding Strategy, Seaspan's Vancouver Shipyards (VSY) hasbeen commissioned to construct and launch a variety of vessels within the Vancouver Shipyards site in North Vancouver, BC, located on the Northshore of Burrard Inlet's Inner Harbour.

Given the space constraints within the VSY basin and in the shipyard, VSY proposes to install approximately 10 monopiles with diameters in the range of 914 mm to 1219 mm (the "Project") to enable the temporary mooring of "store" barges near the final outfitting stages of vessel construction and the shipyard. Six (6) piles will be located along the west side of the pier and four (4) piles along the east side of the pier.

Document.project_name: Phase 2 Polar Icebreaker Dredge Project
Document.description:
Seaspan Vancouver Shipyards (VSY) proposes to dredge approximately 55,000 m³ of sediment within an estimated 21,800 m² footprint at the VSY basin in North Vancouver. Dredging is required to provide additional draft depth and maneuvering clearance necessary to support the outfitting and launch of the new Canadian Coast Guard Polar Icebreaker, which will be constructed under the National Shipbuilding Strategy.

To safely execute the dredging activities and protect existing infrastructure, several enabling works are required:


	Installation of a temporary sheet pile wall to protect an existing remediation mat
	Installation of a new protection marker pile
	Removal of an existing protection pile dolphin


Work activities will be conducted using a barge-mounted derrick equipped with a sealed environmental clamshell dredge bucket, supported by tugs and barges, and other necessary equipment (pile driving equipment).

In-water works will be planned to occur within the Fisheries and Oceans Canada (DFO) least-risk timing window for Burrard Inlet (August 16 to February 28), with dredging expected between November 2026 and February 2027.

Dredged material would be transported for disposal at an approved disposal at sea site under a valid Disposal at Sea (DAS) permit per the Canadian Environmental Protection Act. Any sediments suitable for DAS, will be transported and disposed of at a licensed upland facility.
